ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Chinese Ministry of Public Security's list of politically exposed persons (PEPs). Enhanced due diligence is required for any individual holding a prominent public position in any jurisdiction, including family members and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any material change. The screening process must include name matching with fuzzy logic, date of birth verification, and cross-referencing with adverse media. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. For PEPs, senior management approval is mandatory before proceeding with the incorporation. Additionally, the company must verify that no UBO is subject to any Chinese or international sanctions, and must obtain a written declaration from each UBO confirming their status. The compliance officer must certify the completion of these checks prior to filing the incorporation application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the local State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) name clearance portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters. For foreign names, a phonetic transliteration into Chinese is required. The name must follow a four-tier structure: administrative division (e.g., 'Shanghai'), trade name (unique), industry description (e.g., 'Executive Search'), and legal form (e.g., 'Co., Ltd.'). The trade name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. English names are not registered but may be used for business purposes; however, they must be consistent with the Chinese name in meaning.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (as amended), particularly Articles 1, 98, 100, 108, 129, 387, and 438 governing limited liability companies, absence of minimum capital, director appointment, articles of incorporation, registration filing, and fees; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 7 and 10, for Investment Commission approval and capital verification; Employment Service Act, Articles 4, 34, 35, and 40, plus the Enforcement Rules for Private Employment Service Institutions, for the required statutory license for executive search and headhunting activities
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Company and Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: Taiwan Company Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital; however, the paid-in capital must be reasonably sufficient for the stated executive search business plan, remitted from the foreign shareholder into a Taiwan foreign-investment designated bank account, and evidenced by an Inward Remittance Certificate and a capital verification certificate. No blocked escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company as a limited liability company under the Taiwan Company Act, together with the Articles of Incorporation, is approved in final form and substance. The Company shall register under the exact name [Company Name], and the authorized share capital shall be New Taiwan Dollars [Amount], divided into [Number] ordinary shares of [Par Value] each, all of which have been subscribed and paid fully by the sole shareholder. The paid-in capital shall be remitted to and verified in a Taiwanese Foreign Investment designated bank account, and the capital verification certificate shall be submitted to the Investment Commission and the Department of Commercial Affairs. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the principal place of business and registered office of the Company shall be established at [Address], Taiwan (R.O.C.), and that address shall be the statutory registered office for service of process, notices, and corporate records. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Bank Name], Taiwan, is appointed as the Company's lead banking partner. Any one authorized signatory, identified in the bank instruction card, may execute all banking transactions, including wire transfers, retainer collections, and payments, in accordance with the Company's financial control procedures. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Chairman and statutory representative, [Name] as Director, and [Name] as General Manager and Compliance Officer, each to hold office until resignation or removal by shareholder resolution. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, hire personnel, sign tax filings, and incorporate any necessary subsidiary or branch. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the authorized representatives are directed to file the foreign investment approval application, the company registration application, the tax registration, and the Private Employment Service Institution License application under the Employment Service Act, and to make all necessary declarations and payments. RESOLVED FURTHER, that upon obtaining the employment service license, the Company shall conduct its executive search headhunting business in strict compliance with the Employment Service Act, the Personal Data Protection Act, and anti-money laundering obligations, and shall not commence regulated operations before the license is issued. RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution may be relied upon by any financial institution, government authority, or counterparty as binding corporate authority, and remains effective until expressly amended or revoked by a subsequent written resolution of the sole shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.), and the MOEA Online Company Name Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Foreign Investment Approval Application to the Investment Commission using the official online portal or counter. The application must narrate the ultimate beneficial owner, the exact business scope of C-Suite executive search and technology headhunting, the proposed capital amount and source of funds, and a two-year business plan. The foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the investment, passport copies, and power of attorney must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and, if in English, translated into Chinese by a qualified translator for submission. Simultaneously, reserve the proposed Chinese and English company names through the MOEA online name reservation system to ensure availability for the subsequent incorporation registry filing. The Investment Commission approval letter and the name reservation certificate are preconditions to all later registration steps.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Notarized certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Notarized board resolution authorizing the investment
Passport copy of the ultimate beneficial owner and directors
Two-year business plan for executive search and headhunting
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan filing agent
Proposed Chinese and English company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency notice or suspends the application, respond within 30 days with amended business plan, capital source evidence, or organizational documents. If the application is rejected, the foreign investor may submit a revised application curing the stated defects or file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of the rejection decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-designated foreign exchange bank and Central Bank of China, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the investment approval, the foreign investor must open a foreign-investment designated account at a Taiwanese bank and remit the approved paid-in capital into Taiwan; the remittance may be in foreign currency and converted to New Taiwan Dollars with the bank's foreign exchange transaction record. The bank will issue an Inward Remittance Certificate and a foreign exchange settlement certificate showing the investor's name and purpose. This capital verification certificate is required before MOEA will accept company registration and must evidence that no funds have been withdrawn. The investor should instruct the bank to earmark the remittance as paid-in capital for [Company Name] to align with the approved investment plan. Any change in capital amount or origin requires prior Investment Commission approval before the remittance is accepted.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Bank account opening forms for the foreign investment designated account
Inward remittance instruction and wire transfer confirmation
Foreign exchange transaction record or settlement certificate
Passport and residence certificate of the foreign investor
Approved capital plan from the Investment Commission filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or Investment Commission finds the remittance certificate defective, instruct the bank to issue a corrected inward remittance certificate reflecting the intended capital purpose. If the remitted amount is insufficient, remit the shortfall and obtain a supplementary capital verification certificate. If the exchange rate or remitter identity is challenged, submit the original bank wire confirmation and updated Investment Commission approval letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of a Limited Company with the Department of Commercial Affairs, attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation, appointment of directors, registered office lease, Investment Commission approval letter, name reservation certificate, and capital verification certificate. The incorporation filing must be submitted online or in person, and the statutory representative must affix the original signature or verified seal, attesting to the truthfulness of the filed contents. The Department will examine whether the proposed company name, business scope, corporate governance structure, and share capital conform to the Taiwan Company Act and the approved foreign investment plan. The registration fee of approximately NT$1,000 (about USD 33) must be paid with the application. Once approved, the Department issues the Company Registration Certificate and the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Signed company registration application form
Notarized and translated Articles of Incorporation
Investment Commission approval letter
Company name reservation certificate
Capital verification certificate and inward remittance certificate
Shareholder register and director appointment letter
Lease agreement for the registered office
Power of attorney for the Taiwan filing agent
Certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Commercial Affairs issues a query or suspension, cure the documented defect within 30 days by submitting corrected signatures, translated documents, or a revised business scope. If registration is denied, the applicant may refile after rectifying all compliance gaps and may pursue an administrative appeal before the competent administrative court within 30 days of the denial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Insurance Enrollment, and Private Employment Service Institution License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) and Ministry of Labor Workforce Development Agency, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After company incorporation, the Company must register with the National Taxation Bureau for Value Added Business Tax and uniform invoice issuance, then register as an employer with the labor insurance bureau and the National Health Insurance Administration. The Company must then apply to the Ministry of Labor Workforce Development Agency or the local municipal labor department for the Private Employment Service Institution License under the Employment Service Act. For executive search and headhunting, the application must demonstrate that licensed employment service specialists are employed, a performance bond has been furnished where required by local regulation, professional liability insurance is in force, and a written fee schedule and personal data protection policy have been adopted. The labor authority may conduct an on-site inspection of the office and interview the responsible person and compliance officer. The license must be posted at the place of business and renewed in accordance with the applicable rules.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and establishment application
Business tax and uniform invoice registration forms
Labor insurance and National Health Insurance enrollment forms
Private Employment Service Institution License application form
Certificate of employment service specialist personnel
Performance bond or guarantee letter
Professional liability insurance certificate
Office lease and floor plan for inspection
Fee schedule and internal service contract template
Personal data protection and privacy compliance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the labor authority requests additional documents or identifies noncompliance, submit the requested evidence or cure the deficiency within 30 days. If the license is refused, the Company may re-apply after hiring qualified employment service specialists, completing the bond or insurance requirements, and correcting workplace safety documentation; an administrative review or judicial appeal is available against an unlawful denial.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable: ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting is a pure service activity and does not fall within any Environmental Impact Assessment Act category requiring a full EIA report, project-level assessment, or environmental registration

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (Taiwan's competent tax administration under the Ministry of Finance). Online electronic portal: e-tax Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Complete WFOE incorporation and business registration with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), and obtain the WFOE Business Registration Certificate. 2. Within fifteen days after registration and before commencing operations, file a Tax Registration Application with the competent National Taxation Bureau in the jurisdiction of the registered office, submitting MOEA incorporation approval, articles of association, business registration certificate, Taiwan registered-office address proof, and director/manager identification. 3. The National Taxation Bureau assigns the statutory nine-digit Unified Business Number (UB), which serves as the TIN and Business Tax (VAT) registration ID. 4. Register with the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Turnkey Service for issuing Uniform Invoices, including zero-rated Uniform Invoices for export services. 5. For a foreign non-resident entity operating without a Taiwan permanent establishment, the Taiwan counterparty or statutory agent must perform the applicable simplified Business Tax registration and withhold/pay the Business Tax on cross-border service charges. 6. Maintain the WFOE's payroll, employer tax withholding, and any subsequent change or liquidation registrations through the e-tax Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A WFOE Limited Liability Company is an entity-level resident corporate taxpayer in Taiwan with corporate income tax on worldwide income and Business Tax registration on Taiwan supplies; no pass-through or territorial-scope election is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Taiwan's corporate income tax and Business Tax Act. No check-the-box election, no partnership pass-through election, and no Taiwan hybrid-mismatch election is available for a WFOE limited liability company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No TWD turnover threshold triggers VAT registration. Under the Business Tax Act, any business selling taxable goods or services in Taiwan must apply for tax registration before starting operations. Certain small-scale businesses with monthly sales below the Ministry of Finance's small-scale business standard may qualify for a simplified 1% levy, but registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates a Uniform Invoice regime. Electronic invoices must be issued through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Cloud platform and transmitted to the E-Invoice Turnkey Service using encrypted XML client-to-gateway APIs near real-time. The platform validates invoice numbers and line-item data; it does not pre-approve each invoice with a fiscal stamp. Paper Uniform Invoices remain acceptable without real-time clearance. A zero-rated export service must be evidenced by a Uniform Invoice marked with the zero rate, not the standard 5% rate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to WFOE executive search and headhunting services under Business Tax Act Article 7 when the service is supplied to a foreign client, the service is not consumed in Taiwan, and the WFOE receives consideration in foreign currency remitted from abroad through a Taiwan designated foreign-exchange bank. The service contract, retainer agreement, and final placement documentation must demonstrate that the placed executive is employed in a position outside the Taiwan territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) for any physical goods exported from Taiwan, where applicable
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical cross-border movement where goods are included in the export sales
Commercial Invoice / zero-rated Uniform Invoice clearly marked 0% and referencing the export service
Signed executive search retainer agreement with the foreign client
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (bank-issued inward remittance record) through the Central Bank Foreign Exchange System
Evidence of service performance and overseas usage, including the placed candidate's overseas employer, work location, and final placement report
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating cannot be substantiated, the tax authority will reclassify the sales as 5% taxable supplies, assess underpaid Business Tax, disallow associated input VAT credits, and may impose a surcharge of 5 to 15 times the amount of tax evaded under the Business Tax Act. Fraudulent or unverified zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective clawback, criminal penalty provisions for tax evasion, and the relevant period for assessment extends to the statutory limitation period applicable to Business Tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), supported by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the administering authority for cross-border foreign exchange transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under China's legally administered float and the PRC Foreign Exchange Control Regulations, the yuan (CNY) is convertible for current account items but not freely convertible for capital account items. The WFOE, being a resident entity, may settle service trade receipts (executive search retainers and placement fees) freely with documentary evidence, provided the transactions are genuine and not structured. Capital account operations, including foreign capital injection, shareholder loan repayment, and cross-border profit remittance, are subject to prior SAFE registration, verification, and sometimes quota restrictions. Dividends distributed from after-tax profits may be remitted offshore only after an annual statutory audit and tax clearance; the bank will require the audited financial statements, the tax payment certificates, and the shareholders' resolution. Additionally, the historical requirement to surrender foreign exchange receipts to the central bank has been fully replaced with voluntary retention in foreign currency settlement accounts. The regime is therefore workable for a licensed human-resources firm, but any attempt to convert capital account flows through current account avenues, such as mispriced service fees, would trigger civil and criminal liability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods trade, the current regulations require export proceeds to be repatriated into China within a maximum of 30 days after the customs declaration, and the enterprise can choose to retain the foreign currency in a current account settlement account or settle it into RMB on a market basis; no fixed surrender ratio applies. For service trade (executive search and headhunting), there is no mandatory surrender or fixed settlement ratio; receipts must simply be collected into the WFOE's foreign currency current account through a designated bank and supported by the underlying service contract, invoice, and proof of service completion. All service trade amounts must be reported under the correct trade item and are subject to bank authenticity review.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable. China's licensing regime prohibits offshore digital EMI schemes (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut, or similar) from serving a China-registered WFOE without a domestic bank license or a formal joint-venture with a licensed Chinese clearing bank. No standalone fintech EMI can hold a CNY operational account or execute cross-border RMB settlement; the only lawful rails are the eligible designated foreign currency bank accounts at authorized institutions. Any attempt to route payments through a third-party inline EMI would violate SAFE's 'Real Transaction' principle and expose the entity to account freezing and administrative sanctions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE with a Taiwanese shareholder, the primary statutory person (the legal representative) must generally appear physically in the bank's branch for the initial compliance interview and to execute the account-opening documents. Branches accept an attorney-in-fact in China only if the legal representative's notarized and China-Consulate/Embassy legalized power of attorney is presented, and even then a video interview with the legal representative is mandatory. Fully remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for the capital escrow account, as SAFE rules require on-site verification of the entity's operational capacity and identity of the principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and funding source opacity due to cross-strait investment structure; the ultimate parent in Taiwan is not a public entity and has no audited financial statements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Taiwan company registration certificate and Articles of Association; audited financial statements of every intermediate holding company for the last three years; bank reference letter from the parent's Taiwanese bank; notarized declaration of source of funds; and an organizational chart with full UBO details validated by a certified accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential structuring of service payments to individuals (headhunting fees) that could be used for illegal payroll disbursement or unlicensed money services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of client service contracts and placement agreements with the final employer; invoices for each retainer; proof of completion of executive search (appointment letters, candidate acceptance notices); payroll pass-through prohibition in the internal policy; tax bureau filings showing the agency is not a licensed labor dispatch company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from Taiwan into mainland China is subject to sensitive investment classification; bank may flag the entity as a shell or passive holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration certificate; business license with actual registered office and rent contract; evidence of office space with employee count and payroll; projected service revenue for the first 12 months; and a board resolution proving the injected capital is for operating expenses and working capital, not for margin trades.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual volume of transactions in a low-risk headhunting business inconsistent with reported revenue, potentially indicating conduit activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trailing 12-month bank statements of the parent entity; ERP ledger showing the match between collection and placement milestones; customer counterparty due diligence for each client; and a professional audit trail for every receipt using a standardized invoice scheme.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese parent must first complete SAFE FDI registration for the newly established WFOE, and the WFOE will then open a Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Currency Converted Account) at a licensed bank. The incoming wire must specify the SAFE registration number, remitter name, purpose code 'Investments in Foreign-Invested Enterprises' (code 622), and reference the shareholder resolution. After the transfer arrives, a PRC Certified Public Accountant must issue a capital contribution verification report before any funds can be disbursed. The capital account funds are monitored through the bank's SAFE portal, and every use must be declared against a predefined operational purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service trade disbursements such as sub-agent retainers to overseas search partners or refunds to clients, the WFOE should initiate SWIFT MT103 payments from its foreign current account or RMB basic account. Because executive search services do not involve physical goods, commercial documentary letters of credit and documentary collections are inapplicable; the appropriate clearing rail is the standard wire transfer. Each payment must be backed by an FX purpose code (e.g., 'Service Trade - Commercial and Consulting Services'), the underlying service contract, tax withholding certificate, and any applicable overseas contract fee invoice. Payments must be made to the contracted beneficiary's named corporate bank account, not to a shell or personal account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts (USD/CNY) on a real-demand hedging basis, available only for crystallized current account exposures
FX swaps and currency swaps with a licensed bank, limited to the notional matching the service-trade receivables/payables and approved by SAFE under the 'real transaction' principle

Plain-vanilla FX options purchased on an outright hedging basis (straddles not permitted if speculative); onshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are prohibited for the Chinese WFOE, though the offshore Taiwanese parent can source offshore NDFs independently.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (AGM) resolution approving annual financial statements, business report, and profit appropriation or loss disposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered shareholders in general meeting (internal corporate organ); minutes retained at registered office and exhibited to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and National Taxation Bureau on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year WFOE, on or before 30 June of each year (Taiwan Company Act Article 170)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers are subject to fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 per instance; shareholders may petition the court to convene the meeting; persistent default undermines good-faith management and can lead to administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and statutory business report (annual return/commercial registration filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce - Commercial Registration and Licensure Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year WFOE filing due on or before 30 June; digital e-return portal acceptance closes after the statutory date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA may impose fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000, with successive fines every 30 days for continued default; ultimate sanction is administrative strike-off of the WFOE registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return, including transfer pricing statement and intercompany disclosures if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (jurisdiction over the registered office address)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following tax year; e-filing with transfer pricing statement may carry to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 3% per month on unpaid tax up to 30% plus interest at the postal two-year time-deposit rate; fraudulent understatement attracts penalties up to three times the understated tax and criminal tax-evasion referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bi-monthly Business Tax (VAT) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 15th day of the month after each two-month VAT period (six returns per year; e.g., January-February period due 15 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NT$1,500 to NT$15,000; late payment surcharge of 1.5% for each two-day delay up to 15%; continued delinquency permits collection enforcement and suspension of business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Controller (beneficial ownership) registration update under Company Act Article 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Company Registration Information System (controller disclosure module)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any change involving directors, supervisors, managers, or direct and indirect shareholders holding 10% or more; annual share-transfer reconciliation is completed before the 30 June AGM filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A fine of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 for late or false filing; in egregious cases MOEA may revoke the WFOE's company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Employment Service Institution license renewal and annual self-inspection report (required for ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Labor (Workforce Development Agency) and the local municipality labor department in the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: License renewal every two years, with the renewal application filed at least 60 days before expiry; annual self-inspection report filed on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating beyond permit validity exposes the WFOE to administrative fines of NT$300,000 to NT$1,500,000 and forced suspension; the labor authority may also delist the licensee from the statutory headhunting registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the MOEA audit certification rules, an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandated where any one of the following quantitative triggers is met at fiscal year-end: (i) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 1,000,000); (ii) annual net operating revenue exceeds NT$100 million (approximately USD 3,330,000); (iii) year-end total assets exceed NT$100 million (approximately USD 3,330,000); (iv) year-end bank borrowings exceed NT$30 million (approximately USD 1,000,000); or (v) the WFOE is a parent company required to produce consolidated financial statements. Headcount is not a general audit trigger under Taiwan company law; however, for an ISIC 7830 executive-search licensee, placing 30 or more workers or performing cross-border placements in a calendar year triggers a Ministry of Labor statutory inspection regime requiring a CPA-certified annual statement of service fees and escrowed labor-contract funds, making a certified audit effectively compulsory at that headcount threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS applies to public-interest entities and financial institutions; a private WFOE generally applies Taiwan SME GAAP, the Financial Accounting Standards for small and medium-sized enterprises issued by the Accounting Research and Development Foundation, which is converged with IFRS for SMEs. Group consolidation for a China-parent scenario follows Taiwan-IFRS where required. Tax-basis statements must reconcile to the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act and be prepared under the Commercial Accounting Act, with the audit executed by a licensed Taiwan CPA under the Certified Public Accountant Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan adopts an event-driven controller registration model rather than an annual universal declaration. Under Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must file the controller roster - directors, supervisors, managers, and beneficial owners holding 10% or more - with the MOEA Company Registration Information System within 15 days of incorporation or of any change. At each annual general meeting (due by 30 June), the board must physically reconcile the Register of Members and the recorded controllers, and any resulting shareholding-transfer change must be uploaded to the MOEA system within the same 15-day window. A mere annual confirmation is therefore insufficient; each actual share transfer or officer change opens an independent 30-day statutory reporting window as to the operative 15-day deadline from the change event.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,000 per annum for registered office/address and professional retained-agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per annum for a typical SME WFOE; USD 12,000 - USD 25,000 where Taiwan-IFRS consolidation or transfer pricing documentation is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China applies a standard 25% CIT rate. A 15% reduced rate applies to qualifying High-and-New Technology Enterprises. Small and low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million are subject to an effective rate of 5% (de minimis income aggregation). A 100% additional deduction is available for qualifying R&D expenses. Regional incentives such as 15% preferential rate in Hainan Free Trade Port or Western Region encouraged industries may apply only if the WFOE meets the specific activity threshold. No patent box existed; however, eligible software enterprises may enjoy a 10% reduced rate and corporate tax holidays whereas a generic executive search agency would not be eligible unless an actual China software certification is held for embedded headhunting software.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Category A) Form A100000 with schedules (A105000 related-party transaction adjustments, A109000 affiliated enterprise reporting, and special tax adjustment schedules) filed electronically via the local State Taxation Administration e-Taxation portal (Chinese e-Tax Bureau). Quarterly provisional returns use Form A200000 and are filed online.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional prepayment returns filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return and final settlement of tax are due no later than May 31st of the following calendar year after the tax year-end (December 31). Quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 days from the end of each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from executive search, headhunting retainers, success fees, and any human-resource advisory services derived from Chinese residents or from foreign clients sourced by the China WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include 100% of revenue attributable to the PRC permanent establishment operations. Reject any attempt to reduce revenue by netting intercompany commission income from the Taiwan parent. Revenue attributable to cross-border executive search services must be allocated under the arm's length principle, and invoices must be raised by the WFOE for all PRC-source services. Do not treat fees for services rendered by the Taiwan head office as revenue adjustments absent an actual agency arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs deductible for CIT include researcher salaries, data licensing, advertising, candidate screening fees, and office-related production expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When cost recharges are made from the Taiwan parent, attach a valid cost sharing or recharge agreement evidencing that the fees are at arm's length and the WFOE has actual economic ownership of the services. Costs borne by the WFOE for services provided by the parent for the parent's own benefit are non-deductible. Payment to the Taiwan parent must be accompanied by the annual related-party transactions report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SG&A expenses comprise local property leases, professional fees, information system subscriptions, commission and marketing expenses, and general overhead allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees charged by the Taiwan parent or its regional headquarters shall be disallowed unless the WFOE proves business need and that the expense is directly connected to its income-earning activities in China. The expense must not duplicate expenditure incurred by the WFOE. Allocations must be made under a transparent, contemporaneous methodology acceptable to the PRC tax authority, such as headcount or revenue split per State Administration of Taxation Circulars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record net interest on bank working capital loans, intercompany loans, and guarantee fees, reduced by interest income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on debt owed to the Taiwan parent is subject to thin capitalization limitation of 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises. Any excess interest is non-deductible and is recharacterized as dividend distribution, attracting 10% WHT (7% under the Cross-Strait DTA if properly claimed). Interest remittances require a loan contract registered with SAFE, and withholding at 7%-10% must be made before remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: This is net pre-tax profit according to PRC GAAP on an accrual basis. It is the starting figure for tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The accounting profit must match the audited financial statements. The WFOE should disclose any voluntary transfer pricing adjustments implemented in the accounting book. Underreporting of related-party service revenue from Taiwan clients leads to a complete re-audit of the local appointment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report income exempt from CIT, such as qualifying PRC domestic dividends, grants notified by fiscal regulators, and other de minimis exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE cannot treat cross-border dividends or interest from the Taiwan parent as exempt. Only dividends paid by a PRC resident enterprise to another PRC resident entity qualify for exemption under SAT Circular 83/2014. Intercompany service income may not be reported as exempt income; doing so triggers a false declaration penalty and reclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward of qualifying accounting losses supported by tax vouchers, limited to five tax years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses derived from controlled transactions that are disallowed after a transfer pricing audit cannot be offset in later years. Maintain all loss vouchers and documentation for the duration of carryforward period. Losses cannot be claimed for years when the WFOE conducted no actual business substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all permanent and timing adjustments (accounting profit minus non-taxable income - exempt income + addbacks - deductible items).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable base must include any transfer pricing upward adjustments. Be prepared to reconcile taxable income with the annual related-party transaction disclosure. A loss after TP audit does not relieve the WFOE's reporting obligations under Notice of Special Tax Adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% CIT rate or 15% rate if the enterprise qualifies as a High-and-New Technology Enterprise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident WFOE always pays domestic CIT at the Article 4 rate. The Taiwan parent's DTA status only affects the withholding rate on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties, not the WFOE's calculation of its own taxable income. No foreign tax credit is provided for Taiwan taxes paid by the shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-review line of payments made to the Taiwan parent, including dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees, and status of the annual withholding declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before signing the annual return schedule, verify that all required 10% WHT (or 7%/5% treaty WHT if filing A-form claim) has been withheld and deposited. Where the WFOE failed to deduct WHT on outbound dividends, rectify voluntarily with a late surcharge, otherwise severe Article 69 penalties arise.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return is subject to a fine of RMB 2,000 (up to RMB 10,000 for serious circumstances) under Art. 62 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law plus a daily 0.05% late-payment surcharge. False underpayment returns expose the enterprise to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Art. 63, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Art. 201 of the Criminal Law may result in imprisonment of up to 7 years. The legal representative is subject to exit-control departure bans, joint-action blacklisting, and personal liability if the enterprise fails to collect unpaid taxes after proper enforcement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income, dividends paid to a Taiwan resident beneficial owner may be taxed at 5% if the Taiwan shareholder holds directly at least 25% of the share capital of the Chinese WFOE; otherwise 10% remains. To claim this 5% rate (or the 7% rate for interest/royalties), the party must: (1) obtain a Yearly Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Taiwan tax authority confirming the shareholder's residence; (2) submit the Non-resident Enterprise Treaty Benefits Application (QT) to the Chinese tax authority before the effective withholding date, accompanied by the payment contract, evidence of the direct 25% shareholding, and a Beneficial Owner declaration confirming the recipient is the actual title-holder, not an agent, nominee, or conduit; (3) provide audited financial statements or similar documentation proving no pass-through arrangement; (4) apply to the withholding agent to withhold at the reduced rate; if the application is approved, the WFOE shall withhold 5% on dividends, 7% on interest, or 7% on royalties. If the reduced-rate approval is not obtained prior to payment, the full 10% must be withheld and any overpayment can be reclaimed via a refund application within three years. The Taiwan TRC is issued by the local tax office and must be validated by the mainland tax authority through the cross-strait tax exchange mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding tax on non-resident interest and royalties is 10%. Under the Cross-Strait DTA, interest is reduced to 7% and royalties (including copyright, patent, trademark, secret formula, and software license fees) are also reduced to 7%. The reduced rates require the Taiwan beneficial owner to file a treaty relief application and provide a TRC; payments other than interest, royalty, or dividends, such as technical fees for headhunting services, are not entitled to a reduced WHT unless the WFOE has an economic substance PE in Taiwan, which is generally absent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 40 million in related-party service transactions (e.g., executive search management fees, shared services and commission payments) triggers mandatory Local File preparation. Higher thresholds are RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers/use, and RMB 100 million for financial asset loans. Master File is required when the group's consolidated annual global related-party revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion and related-party transactions in China are recorded. The annual related-party transaction form (A109000) and the summary schedule (A105000) must be filed regardless of amount when any related party transaction occurs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the economic substance doctrine through Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules. The tax authority may recharacterize transactions, disregard entities lacking CIGA, and deny treaty benefits. A WFOE must maintain substantive physical office, full-time qualified staff including the executive search researchers, local decision-making authority in the placement process, independent risk management, and bank accounts in China. Core income-generating activities - candidate sourcing, interviews, background checks, offer negotiation and client relationship management - must occur in China. Where these CIGA remain in Taiwan, the Chinese tax authority will treat the WFOE as a low-risk commissionaire or realize upward transfer pricing to reflect returns to the functions, assets and risks actually borne in China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating fabricated consultant invoices from controlled shell suppliers in mainland China or Taiwan to inflate operating costs of executive search services, or omitting cash retainers and success fee receipts from taxable income, or taking backdated public-fund subsidies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Article 63 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law (TATC): the tax authority shall order the taxpayer to pay underpaid tax plus a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal Law Article 201 imposes criminal liability for tax evasion: a fine and imprisonment of up to 7 years for large evasion amounts exceeding RMB 50,000 after repeated administrative punishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or signed such fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable with the WFOE for tax underpayments under Article 20 of the Company Law (abuse of corporate personality). The legal representative is subject to a border exit ban under TATC Article 44 until taxes, fines, and interest are fully settled. Directors are also listed on the Joint Punishment Memorandum for Tax Dishonesty, leading to a national blacklist affecting credit, banking, aviation and luxury consumption. If criminal amounts are involved, imprisonment up to 7 years applies to responsible directors and CFO.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated success-fee commissions, management fees, royalties or excessive interest to the Taiwan parent or sister entities in a cross-border scheme to shift profits away from China without performing the actual functions, bearing risks, or owning relevant assets; missing contemporaneous TP documentation; or ignoring the 2:1 thin-cap limit on interest deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 44 of the EIT Law and Implementation Regulation Article 123, the tax authority may make a special tax adjustment, recalculating taxable income at arm's length, and will impose late-payment interest of the base rate plus 5 percentage points for failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation. Administrative penalties under TATC Article 63 may amount to 50%-150% of the underpaid tax if the transfer pricing adjustment is based on misreporting; daily 0.05% surcharge continues to accrue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize a transfer pricing scheme that results in underdeclared tax are personally exposed to civil restitution. The Chinese tax authority may pierce the corporate veil if the WFOE is a pure shell performing no CIGA, imposing joint liability on the Taiwan parent. Personal consequences include travel bans, confiscation of luxury assets of the responsible director, inability to leave mainland China pending settlement, and criminal liability for tax evasion in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Profit Repatriation Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest or royalties to the Taiwan parent without withholding the statutory 10% (or reduced treaty rate), without filing Treaty Benefits/QT forms, without obtaining Taiwan TRC, or declaring false Beneficial Owner status; also remitting dividends to a nominee account of an unrelated party to avoid China-source taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Article 37 of the EIT Law and Article 69 of the TATC. The withholding agent is required to pay the amount that should have been withheld, and the tax authority imposes a fine equal to 50% to 300% of the un-withheld amount, plus a daily late surcharge of 0.05%. The non-resident taxpayer remains liable for the underlying tax and may be denied refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who executes the dividend remittance without proper WHT is personally subject to exit restrictions: the tax authority may apply to the court or border police to ban the individual from leaving China until all withholding taxes and penalties are paid. Directors who knowingly used a second-level offshore pass-through to conceal dividend beneficiaries face tax criminal liability; the corporate veil will be pierced to hold the actual controlling directors personally liable to the Treasury for the unpaid WHT, plus civil damages to minority shareholders, and up to 7 years' imprisonment under Article 201.
